summary: Public yeast imaging (IDR: 5 projects and 14 screens; BIA live time-lapse sets) gives cell outlines and budding-pattern phenotypes, and SGD gives categorical budding phenotypes for polarity genes, but no repository dataset reports local surface tension or wall stiffness at the bud site through emergence. The only mechanics deposit found is a 17.5 KB model (Dryad 10.5061/dryad.qjq2bvqn0, CC0) that treats budding as a wall-weakening process.
next_step: Locate the raw data behind AFM / wall-elasticity papers on yeast bud sites (e.g. the thesis 10.18452/20487 and the iScience 2024 article 10.1016/j.isci.2024.110981) or compile a bud-emergence time-lapse with a Cdc42 marker from IDR/BIA and measure curvature; then pre-register the tension-drop vs landmark test.
obstacles_confirmed: Direct local tension reporters are uncommon in archived yeast data: none found in 9 searches.
Phenotype databases record shape and gene, not local tension (SGD CDC42: 'budding pattern: abnormal', no mechanics).
Coverage is excellent for Saccharomyces and thin for other budding yeasts: every hit was S. cerevisiae.
